[SASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781) already learns which historical items matter; its recency behavior alone does not establish the value of an added residual. Proposed controlled ablations: identical backbone with residual exactly disabled through a bypass, verifying baseline scores and gradients; masked uniform mean-pooling residual; last-item embedding residual; fixed-gate recency residual; learned-gate recency residual; and timestamp decay replacing interaction-step decay. Match initialization, batches, optimizer, training duration and checkpoint rules. Normalize residual magnitudes consistently so pooling comparisons isolate weighting. Timestamp decay must use only timestamps available in each prediction prefix.

Separate scale and gradient effects. Include a baseline with a trainable positive logit scale: inference-only scaling cannot change rankings, but training-time scaling changes optimization. Compare the residual with ordinary embedding gradients against the identical forward computation with both history-side and candidate-side residual embeddings detached; keep backbone embedding gradients intact and the gate trainable. This isolates additional gradients entering the shared embedding table. Gate-disabled inference on a residual-trained checkpoint measures dependence on the branch, but cannot replace training the exactly disabled control. These are proposed experiments, not established findings.

Predeclare eight configurations, each covering Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. Use preprocessing seed 0, training/evaluation seed 42, identical 200 validation users/category and 99 unique negatives; select solely by macro HR@10. Fix checkpoint frequency and tie-breaking, cap total search at 43,200 GPU-seconds including diagnostics/failures, and stop without expanding the grid. Report category deltas and paired user-bootstrap uncertainty descriptively. Fixed candidates improve comparability but do not prevent validation overfitting; [sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog model rankings](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651), so restrict conclusions to this benchmark and leave hidden tests untouched.
